blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: Drop the plugin system from this change; the Why (accountants copying invoices into a spreadsheet) is met by a single CSV export. Propose a registry in its own change once a second format is actually requested.
findings.title: Plugin system for future formats is scope nobody asked for

findings.evidence: - A settings page where each user picks their preferred export format.
findings.recommendation: Remove the settings page, its requirement "Users choose their export format" and task 2.1; with a single format there is nothing to choose.
findings.title: Per-user export format preference is scope nobody asked for

findings.evidence: **Alternatives considered**: a single CSV function (not extensible).
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry
findings.recommendation: Choose the single CSV function, which fully answers the Why; extensibility is not a stated need, so it cannot be the reason to reject the simpler option.
findings.title: Design rejects the simple solution only for an extensibility nobody needs

findings.evidence:
- **WHEN** a user picks CSV
- **THEN** exports use CSV
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Users choose their export format
findings.recommendation: If the requirement stays, say which endpoint honours the preference — `GET /invoices.csv` names its format in the path, so "exports use CSV" holds whatever the user picks and cannot fail; otherwise drop the requirement (see R-skeptic-2).
findings.title: Preference scenario has no observable effect: the route hardcodes CSV

findings.evidence: A settings page stores each user's preferred format.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry
findings.recommendation: Either drop the preference (R-skeptic-2), or state where it is stored, the schema change it needs, the default for existing users, and tick `migration` in the Domains.
findings.title: Storing a per-user preference is a hidden schema migration

findings.recommendation: Say who may call `GET /invoices.csv` and add a scenario for an unauthenticated or unauthorized caller; the export returns customer names and totals in bulk, so tick `security` and `personal-data` or give the reason they do not apply.
findings.title: No access-control case for an export of every invoice of a month

findings.evidence: `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM` SHALL return the month's invoices, one per line after a header line, with number, date, customer and total; a field holding a comma, a quote or a line break SHALL be quoted as RFC 4180 says.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Invoices are exported as CSV
findings.recommendation: Fix the header names, the date format and whether the total is in cents (`totalCents` in `src/invoices.ts`) or a decimal amount, so a test can check a line exactly and the spreadsheet reads the numbers.
findings.title: Date and total formats of the CSV are unspecified

findings.evidence: - [ ] 1.2 Plugin registry discovering `src/export/plugins/`, verified by `npm test -- registry`
findings.recommendation: Drop the task with the plugin system (R-skeptic-1); if kept, back it with a requirement and scenarios so `npm test -- registry` checks a specified behavior.
findings.title: Registry task is verified by a test no requirement defines
